{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish at the start. It was a good choice because its outline is smooth, has no sharp corners, and is easy for a judge to recognise. I also laid the start domino and the opening of the top line (stroke 1), which every other stretch grows from. About 33 dominoes of mine went into that line in steady batches. Before the push, the run was traced by eye as connecting 107 of 108 standing dominoes, so nearly the whole picture was set to fall.

Execution: I took one piece of work, the start and the top line, and worked on it steadily. I kept the curves gentle and the joins clean, so the nose and the early top line stayed connected. I inspected the run closely twice, once at about 3:15 and once at about 3:45, to look for gaps. After that I kept my hands off the lines, since extra touching risks bumps.

Collaboration: In the first minute I set out a split of the work: top line, bottom line and tail. I kept clear of the others' areas near the nose to avoid bumps. I said plainly when I would hand a stretch on, and the top line passed to Leo toward the tail without a break.

Leadership: I set the direction early with the fish idea and a clear division of labour. I kept the table focused on smooth lines and on checking the whole run before the push. In the last minutes I kept everyone calm and hands-off.", "my_share_percent": 30}
